title: Cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau: dissipative solitons nucleate from noise and persist, but neither split nor swim in a 30-point scan (new class cgle)
summary: A_t = delta A + (beta + i D/2) lap A + (eps + i)|A|^2 A + (mu + i nu)|A|^4 A with delta=-0.1, D=1, nu=-0.1, integrating-factor Heun on 96^2 (L=40). At eps=0.8, mu=-0.3, beta=0.125, smoothed complex noise relaxes by t~40 into ~15 isolated, phase-rotating pulses that persist to t=300 with constant size and slow repulsive spacing (pack/seed0/sheet.png; 14 and 17 persistent tracks, 0 splits). A scan of eps 0.8-1.8, mu -0.1 to -0.6, beta 0.125/0.3 (scan_*.png, timeseries_4points.png) gives four regimes: the uniform oscillating state riddled with vortex holes (mu=-0.1), isolated pulses (eps 0.8-1.2 with mu -0.3 to -0.6), expanding fronts and stripes (eps 1.2, mu -0.3 to -0.45 at beta 0.3), and amplitude turbulence (eps 1.8, mu -0.6). No pulse split or moved coherently anywhere in the scan; the pulses live on gain from the medium by construction. Worth knowing before anyone tries CGLE for reproduction: it needs a symmetry-breaking or conserved field, not just these coefficients.
